courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at time and space complexity of quicksort.
So we are going to analyze each functions one by one.
Now the first function is swap function.
Now this function swaps the elements in the array.
So this means that the time complexity for swapping the elements is going to be o one.
And the space complexity is also o one, because for this function an additional memory is not required
here, just we are performing the assignment statements which takes O one time complexity.
And the space complexity is also O one.
Now the next function is pivot function.
Now pivot function reorders the array by moving the elements smaller than the pivot to its left and
larger elements to its right, and it also returns the final index of the pivot after rearrangement.
So first we are declaring the swap index variable, which keeps the track of the where the next smaller
element should go.
It starts with the pivot index, meaning that pivot is initially considered in the place.
So the time space complexity for variable assignment is o one.
Then we have this loop.
So this loop iterates through all elements from the one after the pivot to the end index.
So the time complexity for this loop is going to be on in the worst case, because it has to loop through
all elements in the worst case.
And the space complexity is O one because an additional memory is not required over here.
So when it comes to the inside of this loop, we have if condition over here, this condition checks
if the current element is smaller than the pivot.
So this comparison will take O one time complexity.
But the loop itself is on time complexity.
Then inside this if condition we are increasing the swap index by one.
And this will also take O one.
Time complexity and swapping the elements also takes O one time complexity.
So space complexity for this condition also O one.
So when it comes to this swap operation, this one also will take O one time complexity.
Now, if we combine the time complexity for pivot function, it's going to be on time complexity.
And the space complexity is O one.
Now when it comes to the quicksort algorithm itself.
So here we have the base case which will take all one time complexity.
Then we have.
The pivot function is called to partition the array and return the final position.
So this will take on time complexity.
Then we are calling the recursively quicksort function for the left subarray and for the right subarray.
So the time complexity for this call is based on the recursion.
So the time complexity is determined by how well the array is partitioned and leading to either or n
log n time complexity.
For well balanced partitions or n squared time complexity for imbalanced ones.
So this means that in the worst case it's going to take o n squared time complexity.
And it's obvious that the space complexity for recursive call is o n.
So this is applicable for the second recursive call also.
So this means that if we combine everything together, the time complexity for quicksort is going to
be in the worst case or n squared.
But in average and best case it's going to be o n log n time complexity.
And the space complexity in the best case is going to be all again.
And in the worst case it's going to be on space complexity.
